name: VOT2015
description: The Visual Object Tracking challenge 2015, VOT2015, aims at comparing short-term single-object visual trackers that do not apply pre-learned models of object appearance. Results of 62 trackers are presented. The number of tested trackers makes VOT 2015 the largest benchmark on short-term tracking to date. For each participating tracker, a short description is provided in the appendix. Features of the VOT2015 challenge that go beyond its VOT2014 predecessor are: (i) a new VOT2015 dataset twice as large as in VOT2014 with full annotation of targets by rotated bounding boxes and per-frame attribute, (ii) extensions of the VOT2014 evaluation methodology by introduction of a new performance measure. The dataset, the evaluation kit as well as the results are publicly available at the challenge website.
evaluation_method: accuracy (intersection-over-union/overlap) and robustness (failure rate) — composite ranking based on these measures
notes: Non-LLM vision benchmark; uses rotated bounding-box annotations and per-frame attributes. Dataset is relatively small by modern standards which can lead to saturation by state-of-the-art trackers; evaluation emphasizes both overlap (accuracy) and failure rate (robustness).
